Class ServerBehaviorScheduler

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior.ServerBehaviorScheduler
public final class ServerBehaviorScheduler extends Object
The single authority for which eye behavior a mob is playing, and when. Behaviors are cosmetic and client-rendered, but the schedule is server-owned so the "one at a time, non-interruptable" rule holds across every viewer and so server-only game events drive the same path. Triggers are the ambient idle timer below plus game-event reactions (hurt/milked/sheared → grow, trade/heal → swirl, vanilla affection entity events → love). A loose Googly Eye held by a watched entity also gets the holder's hurt (any damage) and heal reactions, per hand (handBehavior(LivingEntity, InteractionHand)). A sleeping mob plays nothing: every trigger is dropped as if the mob were busy, and each client derives the sleeping squint from vanilla's synced sleep state.

Anger is the one ongoing state the scheduler shares, because vanilla keeps it on the server: each tick it checks every ACTIVE mob with OngoingBehavior.serverAngry(LivingEntity) and sends an EyeAngerPacket only when that changes. It never blocks a behavior; the client reddens the pupils underneath whatever plays.

Server-polite: only mobs currently tracked by a player are considered — the tracked set is maintained from StartTracking/StopTracking (so we never scan all loaded entities). A tracked mob always gets a STATES entry (needed for the trackers count regardless of eye state), but serverTick() only walks ACTIVE, the subset that can actually do something: mobs known to have eyes, plus any mob mid-behavior (started via start(LivingEntity, ServerBehaviorScheduler.MobState, EyeBehavior, long), including the debug trigger(LivingEntity, EyeBehavior, long)). A tracked-but-eyeless mob — the overwhelming majority, since the default spawn chance is ServerConfig.GLOBAL_PERCENT — costs one map entry and nothing per tick unless it has a recent held-eye reaction. onEyesGained(LivingEntity) promotes a mob into ACTIVE the moment its eyes turn on (natural spawn already tracked, or a mid-life slimy eye / admin toggle), called from EyeState. A promoted mob that loses its eyes leaves ACTIVE at once (onEyesLost(LivingEntity)), or when the behavior it is playing retires.

A player never tracks themself, yet sees their own eyes in third person, so each player counts as one of their own watchers from the moment they join a level (onPlayerJoined(ServerPlayer)) until they leave or are replaced (onPlayerLeft(ServerPlayer)).

State is per (integrated-or-dedicated) server lifetime; clear() is called on server stop so a single-player JVM doesn't carry one world's mobs into the next. Time is the server's tick count.

    • onEntityEvent

      public static void onEntityEvent(net.minecraft.world.entity.Entity entity, byte eventId)
      The server broadcast vanilla entity event eventId for entity to its viewers. The affection events (an animal entering love mode, villagers breeding, an iron golem offering a flower, an ocelot gaining trust, a pet or horse being tamed) play 'love' if enabled; every other event is ignored.

    • onEyesGained

      public static void onEyesGained(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob)
      Promote mob into the per-tick-walked ACTIVE set now that it's known to have eyes. A no-op if nobody is currently tracking it (no ServerBehaviorScheduler.MobState to promote) — onStartTracking(LivingEntity, ServerPlayer) independently checks EyeState.hasEyes(Entity) for that case. Called from EyeState whenever it synchronizes an eyed mob.

    • onHealed

      public static void onHealed(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob)
      mob is about to be healed: play 'swirl' (if enabled), rate-limited per mob so regen doesn't loop it. Every loader calls this ahead of the heal, on either side, since vanilla also asks a mob at full health to heal. A loose Googly Eye the mob holds swirls too.

    • onEyesLost

      public static void onEyesLost(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob)
      mob no longer has eyes (EyeState synchronized an eyeless state). An idle mob stops being walked each tick at once; one still playing a behavior leaves when that behavior retires.

    • onStartTracking

      public static void onStartTracking(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player)
      A player started tracking mob. Always creates a STATES entry (needed for the trackers count regardless of eye state) and promotes into ACTIVE immediately if the mob already has eyes; a mid-life gain while already tracked comes through onEyesGained(LivingEntity) instead. Also catches the player up if the mob is already mid-effect.

    • onStopTracking

    • serverTick

      public static void serverTick()
      Advance the scheduler one server tick: retire finished behaviors, drop states for removed or unwatched-and-idle mobs, and roll a fresh ambient behavior when a watched eyed mob's cooldown expires. Walks only ACTIVE — see the class doc — so an eyeless tracked mob costs nothing per tick; a mob evicted here is dropped from STATES too, keeping the two in sync.

    • trigger

      public static boolean trigger(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob, EyeBehavior behavior, long seed)
      Try to start behavior on mob now, honoring "one at a time, non-interruptable": dropped (returns false) if the mob is already mid-behavior or asleep. Works even for a mob with no tracking state yet (creates one), so the debug command can drive any looked-at mob.
